problem_statement: Create a list of 5 words. Write a loop that iterates through the list and prints each word alongside its character count. Given Input: words = [\"Apple\", \"Banana\", \"Cherry\", \"Date\", \"Elderberry\"]. Expected Output: Apple - 5 Banana - 6 Cherry - 6 Date - 4 Elderberry - 10.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates whether the algorithm's logic accurately calculates character counts and correctly associates them with each word for all valid inputs.
sub_criteria: The logic correctly determines the character count for any given word.
The algorithm correctly pairs each word from the input list with its corresponding character count.
The loop's conditions ensure that every word in the list is processed exactly once.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses if all required algorithmic components are present, including the input list, the iterative structure, and the output mechanism.
sub_criteria: The pseudocode establishes or refers to the initial list of words as described in the problem.
An iterative structure (loop) is present to process items from the list.
Within the loop, there is a step to access individual words from the list.
The pseudocode includes a mechanism to present the word and its calculated count as output.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates the logical readability and human-understandability of the pseudocode, ensuring clear and unambiguous descriptions.
sub_criteria: The purpose of each step and any intermediate values (like character count) is easily understandable.
The logical sequence of operations for processing each word is clear and straightforward.
The language used to describe the algorithm is plain and avoids ambiguity.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates whether the algorithm avoids obviously unnecessary operations or redundant passes through the data.
sub_criteria: The algorithm processes each word and calculates its length in a single pass through the list.
The algorithm avoids recalculating the length of the same word multiple times.
